AppShellSkeleton.use: AppShellSkeleton is gone: render the frame's Scaffold with placeholder items in its navigation and page, inside a LoadingState.

AppShellSkeletonProps.use: AppShellSkeleton is gone: the frame, a Scaffold, with placeholder items is its loading state.

LoadingBar.use: TopBar's loading and loadingLabel props show page progress along its bottom edge; Progress shows the progress of a task.

LoadingBarProps.use: TopBar's loading and loadingLabel props show page progress along its bottom edge; Progress shows the progress of a task.

useSidebarCompact.use: The sidebar is gone: Scaffold shows a navigation Rail of icons in a medium window, chosen by its width in CSS, with no state to read.

AppShell.use: AppShell is gone. Build the frame on Scaffold: topBar={<TopBar … />}, the navigation forms in navigation={{ bar, rail, drawer }} and the page as its children, as the migration guide's app frame section and the app frame pattern show.

AppShellProps.use: ScaffoldProps and TopBarProps; AppShell is gone. Build the frame on Scaffold: topBar={<TopBar … />}, the navigation forms in navigation={{ bar, rail, drawer }} and the page as its children, as the migration guide's app frame section and the app frame pattern show.

useAppShell.use: AppShell is gone: Scaffold's bodyRef is the element that scrolls the page, and sticky content sticks at the top of the body, at 0.

readAppShellCookie.use: AppShell is gone: a Scaffold keeps no state, since its navigation forms never collapse, so nothing needs a cookie.

AppShellState.use: AppShell is gone: a Scaffold keeps no state, since its navigation forms never collapse.

PerSide.use: AppShell is gone: a Scaffold keeps no state per side.

PersistOptions.use: AppShell is gone: a Scaffold keeps no state; Panes take persist as a localStorage key.

SidebarSide.use: Sidebar is gone: the navigation forms sit at the start or the bottom, and side content goes in a Panes supporting pane.

SidebarSnapshot.use: Sidebar is gone: a Scaffold keeps no state, since its navigation forms never collapse.

FrameStateProps.use: AppShell is gone: a Scaffold keeps no state, since its navigation forms never collapse.

SidebarChangeReason.use: Sidebar is gone: a Scaffold keeps no state, since its navigation forms never collapse.

Sidebar.use: Sidebar is gone: pass the navigation forms to a Scaffold, navigation={{ bar, rail, drawer }}; side content that is not navigation goes in a Panes supporting pane.

SidebarTrigger.use: SidebarTrigger is gone: the Scaffold shows the navigation form that fits its width; open other panels from an IconButton.

SidebarTriggerProps.use: SidebarTrigger is gone: the Scaffold shows the navigation form that fits its width; open other panels from an IconButton.

useSidebar.use: Sidebar is gone: a Scaffold keeps no state, since its navigation forms never collapse.

SplitView.use: SplitView is gone: two panes side by side are Panes.Root with behavior="supporting", Panes.Main, an optional Panes.Divider and Panes.Supporting, as the migration guide's panes section shows.

SplitViewProps.use: Panes.RootProps; SplitView is gone, and Panes.Root takes behavior, splitAt and sizes in rem.

SplitPane.use: SplitPane is gone: two panes side by side are Panes.Root with behavior="supporting", Panes.Main, an optional Panes.Divider and Panes.Supporting, as the migration guide's panes section shows.

ListDetail.use: ListDetail is Panes with behavior="list-detail": v1-structure rewrites its elements.

WindowFrame.use: WindowFrame is gone: a window that draws its title bar is a Scaffold with topBarSpan="full" and topBar={<TopBar titleBar … />}, and bodyRef for scrollRef, as the window frame pattern shows.

WindowFrameProps.use: ScaffoldProps; WindowFrame is gone: a Scaffold with topBarSpan="full" and a TopBar with titleBar frame the window.

TitleBar.use: TitleBar is gone: <TopBar titleBar start={…} title={…} actions={…} />, with its end content in actions.

TitleBarProps.use: TopBarProps; TitleBar is gone: a TopBar with titleBar is the window's title bar.

AccountMenu.use: AccountMenu is gone: build the account menu from Menu.Root with an AvatarButton trigger, a Menu.Header with the Avatar and the name, and a Menu.Submenu around a ThemeRadioGroup, as the account menu pattern shows.
